the_bar: sqrt(2) x threshold (PROTOCOL A26). The 'equals float64' threshold is unreachable for any bf16 port: two independent error vectors of equal size subtract to sqrt(2) times one of them. Scoring a bf16 port against the unreachable threshold manufactures a failure, which the campaign did for 174 passes.
the_deepest_finding: every disagreement we measure is GEOMETRY, not an unexplained defect. With q = ||our error|| / ||their error|| and the cosine between the two error vectors, ||e-t||/||t|| = sqrt(q^2 + 1 - 2q cos) predicts all three measured scopes to within 1.26e-05, across a range spanning 129x. So 'do we reproduce training' reduces entirely to two measured quantities per scope. And it has a consequence that cost a row 35 % of its own error to demonstrate: past ||e|| ~ ||t||, getting MORE accurate does not get you closer to the reference -- bounding five more verbs in float64 removed 35 % of our error and bought 0.57 % of agreement.

THE_TRUNK_SCOPE_IS_SETTLED_NO_GO_pass_18.and_it_is_a_conclusion_not_a_null: the row did not merely fail to find the amplifier -- it showed there is none to find. The single-block backward error does grow with depth, by 13840x in the single-track cotangent across seven boundaries. Divide each depth by ITS OWN pure-bf16 floor and the growth is gone: 1 - cos(dL/ds_in) over its own floor reads 1.46, 218, 74, 32, 28, 99, 103 at blocks 0, 8, 16, 23, 32, 40, 47, Spearman +0.32 against depth. The depth dependence in the raw number IS THE FLOOR'S depth dependence -- this cotangent becomes ill-conditioned in bfloat16 as the stack deepens, for upstream as much as for us -- and our excess over it is a roughly constant factor that does not order by depth.
THE_TRUNK_SCOPE_IS_SETTLED_NO_GO_pass_18.the_preregistered_test_and_how_close_it_: DIFFUSE on both dependents. Best candidate ||s_in|| reaches Spearman 0.857 on ours/floor and 0.893 on the direction deficit, against the 0.929 fixed in advance. The row honoured its own threshold rather than rounding 0.893 up to 'tracks'.
THE_TRUNK_SCOPE_IS_SETTLED_NO_GO_pass_18.why_no_rho_could_have_settled_it: ||s_in|| is monotone in depth over these boundaries, so depth and norm are RANK-IDENTICAL and a rank test cannot separate them at any rho. And ||s_in|| jumps 239x between block 0 and block 8 then moves 1.57x over the whole of blocks 8..47 while the deficit moves 1165x -- block 0 is the only low-norm point on the ladder, so the apparent norm relationship rests on n=1 at that end. The instrument I specified could not have answered the question whichever way the number fell; that is a defect in my brief, not in the row's execution.
